I've added the following content to the post-merge hook:

```bash
#!/bin/bash

# Post-merge hook to push master branch to secondary public remote
# This script runs automatically after a git merge operation

# Check if we're on the master branch
if git branch --show-current | grep -q "^master$"; then
    echo "Post-merge: Detected master branch. Attempting to push to secondary remote..."
    
    # Check if secondary remote exists
    if git remote | grep -q "^public$"; then
        # Push master branch to public remote
        git push public master
        if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "Successfully pushed master branch to public remote"
        else
            echo "Failed to push to public remote"
            exit 1
        fi
    else
        echo "Secondary remote 'public' not found. Please add it with: git remote add public <repository-url>"
    fi
else
    echo "Post-merge: Not on master branch, skipping push to secondary remote"
fi
```

The script checks if the current branch is master, verifies the existence of a remote named "public", and pushes the master branch to it if both conditions are met. If the public remote doesn't exist, it provides instructions for adding it. The hook will run automatically after each merge operation.
